steps.title: Measure and watch the bursts build up
steps.text: The Record tool measures single molecules (Point) or scans an image (Image) and analyses the data while the measurement runs. Every part sits in its own window -- Acquisition, Laser, Analysis, Quality and one per plot -- which you can dock, tab, float, resize and fold; Start, Stop and Laser off stay in the bar on top. Until a device is connected it measures the simulator.

steps.title: Load the example
steps.text: Point mode (the default) measures single molecules at one spot. The example: two populations with E 0.2 and 0.8, both at stoichiometry S 0.5, measured with the default PIE setup.

steps.title: Point or Image
steps.text: Mode chooses a single-molecule measurement at one spot (Point: bursts, E–S, the running trace) or a scan (Image: the image builds up line by line, molecules are picked on it and measured one by one). Keep Point for now; the tour comes back to Image at the end.

steps.title: Pick the measurement type
steps.text: The Measurement type decides what is computed and shown: PIE and ALEX give proximity ratio and stoichiometry (the E–S histogram), two colour the proximity ratio, MFD anisotropy, single colour burst size and duration. 'From the setup' takes the type the Instrument setup describes.

await.hint: Choose the Measurement type ('From the setup' is fine for the example).

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Photons are analysed as they arrive and written to the recording at the same time.

steps.title: Watch the histogram
steps.text: Each finished burst lands in the type's histograms -- for the PIE example two clusters at E 0.2 and 0.8, both at S 0.5; Histogram picks which is shown.

steps.title: The running trace
steps.text: The last second of photons in 1 ms bins: the donor under donor excitation up (green), the acceptor down -- FRET (red) and directly excited acceptor (magenta). A FRET burst is a green spike over a red one. Span and bin width are in Analysis › Running trace.

steps.title: Decays
steps.text: The micro-time decays of each detector over the micro-time channels, with the excitation windows marked. During the run Record finds the excitation pulses in these decays: when the windows do not hold them, the detected edges are drawn in orange and the Experiment setup panel offers Update windows or Keep -- you decide; the run goes on.

steps.title: Read the traffic lights
steps.text: The FRET quality checker judges the bursts so far, every two seconds: the overall light is the worst check. Green: continue. Amber: usable, read the note. Red: act now — the note says what to do (dilute when the occupancy is too high, check background, focus or laser power). The lights stay grey until there are enough bursts for a verdict. The verdict at stop is stored with the run.

steps.title: Stop
steps.text: Stopping closes the open burst and the recording. The recording enters the Datasets workspace as a photons dataset, its bursts as a run below it — ready for Burst Selection, ndXplorer and the other burst tools, with exactly the bursts you saw.

await.hint: Press Stop (or wait for the duration to pass).

steps.title: The laser button
steps.text: One button for the laser: red Laser off while it emits blocks all emission at once (always there, never fails); green Laser on switches emission on once a program is applied. The end of a run closes the excitation shutter; the laser itself is not touched.

steps.title: Arrange the windows
steps.text: Drag a window's title to float it or dock it elsewhere (several in one place become tabs), resize it from any edge, double-click a title to fold it. Reset layout puts everything back.

steps.title: Image: scan a sample
steps.text: Switch Mode to Image (scan). With a TCSPC device and the scanner of the settings file (the MT200's PI E-725) the device records the scanner's line markers while it rasters; without hardware the simulator scans a sample.

steps.title: Load the image example
steps.text: Single molecules on a coverslip (a few spots hold two), 64 × 64 pixels of 100 nm, four frames.

steps.title: Scan
steps.text: The image builds up line by line in the Image window, from the line markers in the photon stream.

await.hint: Press Start and wait for the four frames.

steps.title: Auto-pick the molecules
steps.text: Auto-pick runs the spot finder's single-molecule workflow on the intensity image and adds the molecules it finds as points, brightest first (Max molecules, Min/Max photons limit it). Each point gets a numbered ring on the image and a row in the table.

steps.title: Or pick by hand
steps.text: A click on the image (not a drag, which pans) adds a point at that stage position; ✕ in a row or Delete removes one.

steps.title: Measure the points
steps.text: The focus parks on each point in turn and the device records it -- for Time per point, or less with Until bleached: a point ends once its count rate has stepped down to the background. Each point is a recording of its own in Datasets.

steps.title: The molecule's trace
steps.text: While a point records, Trace shows its count rate per detector with the bleach threshold (dashed) and the moment the rule called it bleached, and under it the FRET efficiency and the mean arrival time per bin.

steps.title: Each molecule's results
steps.text: After each point its trace is segmented into states (the intensity-trace tool's binning and the shared HMM): bleaching steps, bleach time, photons, E before any bleaching and a fast lifetime fill its row. Select a row: its trace and HMM path appear in Trace and its ring is highlighted. The table is stored with the image.

steps.title: Survey a larger area
steps.text: Open Survey in the Points window: it does all of the above by itself, tile after tile -- image a tile (the Scan panel's raster; the tile is Width × Height), Auto-pick, Measure points, move on -- until Stop, a stop condition or the whole area (by default the scanner's whole range) is done. Tiles without molecules are passed.

steps.title: Start the survey
steps.text: The tiles spiral outward from where you focused (a coverslip is rarely flat: the nearest tiles are the best focused). The shutters open once and close when the survey ends; Stop keeps everything measured so far.

steps.title: Follow it on the map
steps.text: Each tile in the order it is visited: orange now, green measured, dark empty, red failed; dots are measured molecules. Tile, molecules, elapsed time and the time left are on the line above; the log is the tooltip of the line under the map. One table of all molecules is stored with the first tile's image.

steps.title: The camera
steps.text: The Camera dock previews a camera or capture card next to the plots -- in every mode, including the simulator, because it watches the sample, not the photons. Enter a camera index, a Matrix Vision device (mv:0) or a file, press Connect, and judge the coverslip distance from the backreflection; Preview gain brightens a dim feed without touching recordings. Recording to a name ending in .tif or .tiff writes every frame to a multi-page TIFF; any other name needs the optional OpenCV package.
